note: Hover definitions for the player site wiki. Player-safe: only what the handouts already say. 'match' lists the exact words that get the definition (case-sensitive, whole words); 'entry' is the wiki entry it links to when that entry is public.

terms.text: A Court-licensed memory assayer: the only person allowed to draw a memory out of someone, with a tuning fork, and only with their consent.
The office on the Tally where Reckoners buy and sell memories. The day's rate is posted on a slate by the door.
The most valuable sealed memory: a defining one, like a parent's face or a wedding day. Worth 25 to 100 gold pieces.
The smallest sealed memory: a passing moment. Worth about a silver piece in Pellmoor.
The Quiet Court's tax, paid in memories. A Tithed memory goes into a jar in the Court's vaults.
Paying a Corvanese person's Tithe in gold for them. Illegal, and it happens every day.
Someone who has given away so many memories they no longer know their own family.
What ringing a bell costs the person who rings it: a memory, a year, a sense, a name, a fear or a gift. You always hear the price first.
The bronze clapper that makes a bell ring. A bell without its Heart is silent.
An officer of the Quiet Court. Grey silence-stone gloves that muffle their own blows. Very quiet.
The government, ruled from Hallowmere. It believes the bells must never ring again.
Corvane's own church. It worships the Silence and calls the Faerûnian gods "the loud gods."
A grey stone the Court uses to stop magic. Spells fail within about ten feet. It can be smashed or carried off; dispelling won't help.
What Corvanese call magic. Every spell hums faintly as it is cast.
What Hushmen call loud magic inland. It draws their attention.
Hallowmere's own knights, sworn to Vaer by old tradition. They keep watch under a sky that never brightens.
A secret network of bell-makers and tuners, outlawed and hunted for three hundred years. They want the bells rung.
The restless dead of the Mute Mere, singing their grief. They want to be remembered by name.
The old families of Pellmoor. They pilot every foreign ship across the drowned town.
The horse-clans of the northern steppe. Proud, blunt, and wary of anyone after their bronze.
A Faerûnian who has settled in Pellmoor for years.
The polite word for a Faerûnian newcomer. The rude one is "Loudfolk."
The rude word for Faerûnians. The polite one is "Stormborn."
What Faerûnians call people born in Corvane.
The land's own name for itself, and its language.
Years "since the Silence." 412 SS is 1492 DR.
The night, 412 years ago, when every bell in Corvane fell silent at once.
The one-night storm in 382 SS that came up the river onto the Mere, drowned people, and left the Seam open behind it.
The permanent band of storm, thirty to sixty miles deep, that circles Corvane at sea.
The one calm lane through the Stormwall, at the mouth of the river Pell. Every ship takes a pilot.
The Court paper a foreigner needs to travel inland past the Mere road.
The Court's customs office on the Quays: the landing fee, registration and writs of passage.
Where ferry-folk pilots are hired. No ship crosses the drowned town without one.
A stretch of the Old Shore where the names of the drowned are scratched on stones.
The vast, perfectly still lake with a drowned town beneath it. Its water remembers the dead.
